description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a large language model’s response to external feedback, as studied in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.81 to 0.99 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major ticks every 0.2. The “Final Accuracy” (blue line with circle markers and solid line) remains consistently high, hovering near 0.95–1.0 across most of the confidence range, with slight dips around 0.82 and 0.95. The “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and dashed line) starts at approximately 0.55 at 0.81 confidence, dips slightly, then rises steadily to nearly 0.95 by 0.99 confidence. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange line with diamond markers and dashed line) shows the change in accuracy after feedback; it begins around 0.45 at 0.81, drops sharply to near 0.1 at 0.89, then fluctuates with a small peak near 0.93 before declining again toward 0.05 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements, with larger error bars for Δ Accuracy, especially at lower and higher confidence values.
